title: Classify all ten shortest binary depth-six chain schedules (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

The unsigned depth-six dirty chain has exactly **ten** shortest universally correct schedules in characteristic two. They are precisely the ten distinct cyclic rotations of `(1234565432)^2`. Every adjacent pair is noncommuting in the universal alphabet, so no shortest schedule permits a local commuting-neighbor retiming move.

```text
known minimum: 20 complete calls
new classification: 10 shortest schedules = 1 cyclic-rotation class
                    10 separate classes under commuting-neighbor swaps
```

Claim type: **exhaustive finite computation / finite certificate**, with a scoped algebraic reduction. No new kappa or supplier admission.

The length 20 is already implied by Yifan Kang's [CNOT-Optimal Circuit Synthesis, Proposition 3.1](https://math.mit.edu/documents/rsi/2023KangY.pdf), and is not claimed as original. The new result is the complete schedule classification and its retiming consequence. Only `research/depth6-binary-chain/` is added.

Produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Nick Petalas's #4249/#4263/#4281 for the chain model and interval-count reduction, Ryanson Jonathan's #4418 for the separate depth-five residue successor, and Ross Richardson's #943/#934 complete-call connector lineage. These predecessors are cited, not re-audited. The [advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19130783) and [scope update](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19130859) distinguish the known minimum from the new classification.

## Evidence

- Before: the directed-path minimum supplies an attaining construction and call-count lower bound, without this complete depth-six schedule classification.
- After: complete BFS in the `2^21`-state `UT7(F2)` graph, exact forward shortest-path counts, and separate backward enumeration using full 7-by-7 matrix products all identify the same ten words. No search pruning is used. The target is absent among the 1,197,817 states through level 19 and first appears at level 20.
- All ten words pass chronological interval counts and full matrix products. Across them, 81,920 scalar dirty map/state cases and 8,960 two-coordinate dirty replays pass. The transition oracle passes 132 affine-basis comparisons, and six deliberately invalid controls are rejected.
- Both registered warning-strict normal/optimized commands pass locally on CPython 3.12.15, NumPy 2.5.4, macOS arm64. Timed direct checks took 0.425 s and 0.520 s, below their 120-second limits. Receipts are generated from every package/input hash.
- `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` including source-history ancestry, and the eight-file committed export integrity check pass at `fc09e5b783989d769e6ae6fffeb7d23b30177c86`. Both isolated normal/optimized Git-free export replays pass.


Any CPython 3.12 interpreter with the declared NumPy version can replace the local path. Every registered mathematical check was run locally; no opt-in mathematical obligation is omitted.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The result covers this depth, characteristic, universal complete-call alphabet and shortest length only. It does not classify longer words, other depths/characteristics, or schedules under additional map-specific identities. Bounded Python/NumPy allocation is documented. No physical caller, routing, dispatch, precision, tape/storage, recursive supplier or outer multiplication proof is supplied. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No selected-frontier change, Lean build or selected cold replay is part of this package.

## Open next questions

1. Derive the complete chronology constraints structurally from the known minimum count vector, and determine whether rigidity persists at other depths.
2. Find the least extra call budget permitting nontrivial commuting retiming after adjacent equal-call cancellation. Reduced length 22 is the first bounded test.
3. Identify an actual six-stage consumer and price its complete physical boundary before interpreting these schedules as recursive savings.

## Related open work

- #4600 studies balanced depth-four short-row obstructions over all moduli. This package studies complete shortest depth-six binary words; no common depth/coefficient count is asserted, so no overlapping number requires a numeric comparison.
- #1930 constructs persistent prefix outputs without restoring the intermediate rows. Its output contract differs from this restored-intermediate chain; its three-call value is not a value for the target classified here, and there is no shared numerical claim.

Merged #4418 decides separate depth-five residues. The original scope was explicitly changed after the external known minimum was identified. Fresh overlap covered all 506 open PR records and 3,669 Discussion records with complete reported pagination at 2026-10-22 19:02 UTC. Local cached-note coverage was sparse; additional direct main-README searches and merged-PR searches covered the distinctive word, shortest-schedule count and chain object. This is an overlap report, not a guarantee of novelty.

Before DONE, this account's open PRs created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-22 18:54:13 UTC were refreshed. Apart from this PR:

- #4745 classifies square-zero radical right-vector targets. Its reachability counts concern a different alphabet and target, with no numerical schedule-count overlap.
- #4746 proves a prescribed-product Schur dimension theorem. Its dimension and rank quantities do not overlap this schedule classification.
- #4747 gives a corank-one pair full-guard header law. Header probabilities differ from these chain-word counts; no numerical overlap is asserted.
- #4749 proves an invertible semilocal right-vector cost formula. Its factor alphabet and targets differ from this six-call chain, with no numerical overlap.

No newly opened account PR studies the same depth-six schedule object or quantity. The earlier related chain work remains listed above.
